entries.targeted_claims: Table interpretation, rank conventions, selected global forms, dimension fields, and low-rank examples.
entries.evidence: Read the whole guide. Checked the table convention rather than asserting all Lie groups or all real forms are classified. Real dimension doubles for a complex vector-space tangent algebra; SL(2,C) has complex dimension 4-1=3. SU(2) and Sp(1) have real dimension3. The selected classical matrix groups and exceptional adjoint split forms are explicitly distinguished from topological universal covers.

entries.targeted_claims: Complex symplectic matrix-size notation and equality of compact/split real dimensions.
entries.evidence: Complex realization is Sp(2n,C) intersect U(2n) with matrix-size indexing. Compact Lie algebra has3n real diagonal parameters and4*n*(n-1)/2 off-diagonal parameters, totaling n(2n+1). Split symplectic blocks have n^2+2*n*(n+1)/2=n(2n+1) parameters. Different real forms do not imply different real dimensions. Other existing claims remain outside this targeted review.

entries.targeted_claims: Separate n=1 trivial case from n>=2 noncompactness.
entries.evidence: For n=1, determinant-one real1-by1 matrices are exactly{1}, so compact and simply connected. For n>=2, diag(t,t^-1,1,...,1), t>0, is unbounded, proving noncompactness. Existing simple-connectivity claims for n>=2 are unchanged and not newly certified by this elementary check.
